sections.kicker: Prepared for Mister Zimi by Atla · November 2026
sections.lead: We looked at your site and your Instagram the way a new customer would. Here is what stood out, in order of weight.
sections.thesis: Mister Zimi has a line worth owning. The grid says it less often than the bio.
sections.keep: Your bio line, Your Everyday Holiday. It is short, it is yours and it says what the clothes are for.

sections.label: Front door
title: Three things people
meet first.
Three things
people meet

pins.what: The bio line is a real position: holiday clothes for ordinary days.
pins.why: It answers why Mister Zimi and not the resort label next door.
pins.how: Let that line steer the captions and the grid, so the idea shows up outside the bio.
pins.label: Your bio
pins.cost: The idea stays one line while the grid sounds like any fashion label.

pins.quote: A very important meeting. Agenda: lunch, debriefs, another round.
pins.what: One caption speaks in the brand's own voice.
pins.why: Most captions announce something. This one sounds like a person on holiday, the only one that sounds like Everyday Holiday.
pins.how: Write every caption in this voice and let announcements follow it.
pins.label: Your caption
pins.cost: The voice that sets the brand apart appears once.

pins.what: The bio says Australia. The tiles look like holiday streets abroad.
pins.why: Where the brand comes from is part of why it is different, and it never appears.
pins.how: Show the Australian starting point once: a beach, a street, the studio.
pins.label: Your grid
pins.cost: The brand reads as any resort label made anywhere.

sections.intro: You asked for a look at Mister Zimi. I spent some time on your Instagram. Three things stood out.
